newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen Stahl to slash loss carryover.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen Stahl to slash loss carryover.

text.p: Thyssen Stahl AG, Germany's largest steel maker, said on Thursday it aims to eliminate entirely its loss carryover.
In the 1995/96 business year to September 30, the Thyssen AG unit's loss carryover totalled 968 million marks, down from 1.553 billion marks the year before.
Chief executive Ekkehard Schulz declined to give a specific timeframe for cutting the loss carryover, but said it would have a significant impact on the company's net profitability.
Schulz declined to make a specific forecast for net profit in the current year.
"It will not be as good as in 1994/95" when Thyssen Stahl posted a record 651 million mark profit, Schulz told reporters.
"But I do not want to say now if it will be as good as 1995/96," when profit dropped to 174 million marks, he added.
Thyssen Stahl is in the midst of a restructuring in which it will shed non-core activities and concentrate on hot-rolled products.

It aims to reduce its parent work force to 13,600 by the end of 1998 from 16,900 on September 30, 1996. It wants to cut its work force in flat-steel products to slightly above 10,000 by the year 2000 from 12,800 currently.
The group's overall workforce was 35,990 in September 1996, down from 39,572 a year earlier.
The company plans further international downstream tie-ups that will build its sales to 12 billion marks by the year 2000 from 10.623 billion in 1995/96.
The company plans to sell off non-core activities with total sales of one billion marks that showed a net loss of 100 million marks last year, Schulz said.
